sentences.text: Collaborative target time management establishes a shared operating baseline for each departure by linking the Target Off Block Time, the Calculated Takeoff Time, and the key surface milestone timestamps to the same flight record.
The Regional Flow Platform creates the initial Target Off Block Time proposal from current flight intent, stand readiness, turnaround progress, and applicable airport capacity constraints.
The Demand Prediction Service estimates demand pressure over the next planning horizon and marks flights whose proposed Target Off Block Time values are likely to cause runway or sector imbalance.
The Capacity Assessment Module applies the active Airport Capacity Plan and Airport Acceptance Rate to determine whether the proposed demand pattern remains operationally feasible.
The Slot Allocation Engine derives the Calculated Takeoff Time by combining runway metering constraints, departure fix loading, and applicable Ground Delay Program rules.
The Tower Sequence Manager maintains the tactical runway sequence expectation and highlights cases where the Calculated Takeoff Time is inconsistent with the local departure order.
The Ramp Movement Board maintains milestone timestamps for stand readiness, boarding completion, doors closed, start approval readiness, taxi start, and other locally configured departure events.
The Time Synchronization Service provides the reference clock for all target time calculations so that negotiation records and operational timestamps can be compared without local clock ambiguity.
For voice coordination, Halcyon is the operational call sign used by the Slot Coordinator during daily target time conferences.
The Slot Coordinator reviews proposed Calculated Takeoff Time values against network constraints and requests adjustment when the allocation would create avoidable delay or unfair sequencing.
The Airline Operations Coordinator reviews the proposed Target Off Block Time against aircraft readiness, crew availability, passenger connection risk, and operator recovery priorities.
Saffron shall confirm any operator-requested Target Off Block Time revision in the Airport CDM Portal before the freeze horizon expires.
The Ground Handling Dispatcher updates handling milestones when service completion forecasts change, and those updates are treated as negotiation inputs until the freeze point is reached.
The Ramp Control Lead assesses whether the proposed off-block pattern is compatible with apron access, stand conflicts, and local movement restrictions.
The Tower Supervisor may challenge a proposed Calculated Takeoff Time when runway configuration, wake spacing, or local sequencing conditions make the value operationally unsuitable.
The Airport CDM Portal presents each proposed value with its confidence status, last update time, and the reason code assigned by the proposing function or authorized user.

The Common Situation Display shows the current agreed target set so that operational participants can see whether a flight is proposed, under negotiation, frozen, or exempted from compliance monitoring.
Negotiation remains collaborative while the value is outside the freeze horizon, and each accepted amendment replaces the prior value as the current shared plan.
The Collaborative Decision Log records each challenge, counterproposal, acceptance, rejection, and reason code associated with the Target Off Block Time and Calculated Takeoff Time.
At the configured freeze horizon, the Regional Flow Platform locks the Target Off Block Time unless a rule-based exception or an authorized operational override is recorded.
A frozen Calculated Takeoff Time may still be revised when the Slot Allocation Engine receives a capacity update that changes the feasible departure allocation for the affected traffic set.
When a frozen value changes, the Airport CDM Portal requires a revised reason code and marks the earlier value as superseded rather than deleted.
The Audit Event Ledger stores the previous value, new value, responsible user or automated function, timestamp, authority basis, and applicable operating state for every target time change.
The Identity Access Service ensures that only users with the assigned operational role can approve frozen-time changes, manual exemptions, or retrospective corrections.
The Data Governance Steward reviews audit samples to confirm that timestamps are complete, reason codes are valid, and manual changes can be traced to an operational justification.

The Performance Analytics Warehouse uses frozen targets, actual milestone timestamps, and audit records to measure compliance, delay attribution, negotiation effectiveness, and rule quality after operations.
